components.name: Character Maker
components.summary: The core editing path works for selected normal characters.
components.available: Normal male/female cards, asynchronous head 0/200/201 and converted asset selection, shape and color edits, static ABMX, and identity-preserving edited exports. Bounded decoded-rig reuse accelerates repeated normal-head selections while retaining actual byte verification.
components.remaining: Wider catalogs, special and modded assemblies, complete original editing workflows, and remaining owner-thread stalls. First selections still decode and now pay hashing/accounting costs.
components.evidence: In a small Release pair, median warm normal-head selection fell from 667–701 ms to 159–161 ms. First selections cost 16–25 ms more. Logical retained rig payload reached about 39 MB; this is not total RAM or a whole-app benchmark.

components.name: Base Models
components.summary: Six normal assemblies have bounded original-player comparisons.
components.available: Female and male heads 0/200/201 have independent neutral and one coupled-shape gates. Head 0 also has bounded bone-type-1 checks for both sexes.
components.remaining: Other corrected types, arbitrary shapes, complete hierarchy, animation and appearance parity. Passing selected vertex and binding checks does not establish full-character parity.
components.evidence: The owning reference records exact model identities, tolerances, original/native hashes and independent neutral repeats.

components.name: Base Shapes
components.summary: Recovered shape rules drive a bounded set of native controls.
components.available: 52 face and 44 body controls with recovered destination and ordering rules, numerical gates, and the source fixed-height rule for normal male Maker models.
components.remaining: Broader model/shape combinations and unsupported transform cases. The control count is not a universal parity claim.
components.evidence: Independent model gates cover selected coupled edits; individual kernel results and complete assembled-model results remain distinct.

components.name: Renderer
components.summary: Native toon rendering and an opt-in source-shader path are usable.
components.available: Metal rendering, explicit toon fallbacks, resource ownership and caching, and live translated source shaders in selected Studio scenes.
components.remaining: Remaining material dispatch, original scene effects, resource limits, and representative displayed-scene performance acceptance.
components.evidence: Allocation reductions and functional passes are recorded separately from timing. Source-shader rendering remains opt-in.

components.name: Materials
components.summary: Selected native composites pass independent image gates.
components.available: The controlled fixture reaches 19 of 20 live material slots, including the verified female head-0 face composite with null selected layers. Independent base/distinct face targets pass the one-byte gate.
components.remaining: Body remains an explicit fallback. Other heads, makeup layers, patterns, states and whole-character shading remain open.
components.evidence: 19/20 describes one controlled fixture. Added face coverage raises GPU work and memory; six default-OFF captures match the accepted controls. Full source-color parity is not established.

components.name: Visual Fidelity
components.summary: Selected geometry and image checks pass; full-scene parity is open.
components.available: Bounded geometry, pose, material and matched-frame gates, plus independently evaluated live comparisons and sampling diagnostics.
components.remaining: Full-character silhouette and color parity, and repeatable same-input live sampling. Discard and explicit-gradient experiments are diagnostic evidence, not production fixes.
components.evidence: Frozen geometry, recovered-code oracles and original-player comparisons prove different things; each gate names its reference.

components.name: Mods
components.summary: Immutable indexing and selected asset resolution preserve identity.
components.available: Incremental archive/profile indexing, saved-ID resolution, converted selections, static ABMX and unknown-payload preservation.
components.remaining: General mod geometry, dynamic callbacks, migrations and installation-wide compatibility. Preserved data does not imply executable support.
components.evidence: Resolved catalog identity and byte-preserving round trips are bounded to the documented input formats and versions.

components.name: Plugins
components.summary: A useful bounded execution subset exists; general compatibility is early.
components.available: Translated profiles and three exact-revision native adapters: Mute, StudioAccessoryNames and HideAllUI. Selected mount, cancellation, failure isolation and save/restore workflows are exercised. Native save/reopen now retains queued destruction roots without replaying Awake. Rejected frames restore exact route history, including irregular time steps and lazy-clock ownership.
components.remaining: General DLL, Harmony, coroutine and Unity compatibility, original save adapters, and broader lifecycle coverage. Initialization that changes candidate topology is rejected; library installation retains a separate attachment-read boundary.
components.evidence: Saved-profile restoration permits candidate-owned attachment reads only when initialization leaves the candidate scene unchanged. Metadata inventory does not establish loadability. The queued-destruction change passed 34 Engine tests and 222 app checks in its recorded acceptance. Exact route rollback passes 11 Engine tests and 88 Release app checks; checkpoint timing cost remains unmeasured.

components.name: Studio & Scenes
components.summary: Selected source scenes can be viewed and edited.
components.available: Original characters, cameras, FK/IK, animation, expression/shape/outfit/accessory edits, reachable Pose/Face/Clothes inspectors, and bounded scene export.
components.remaining: Broader interactive acceptance, mixed scene objects, maps, lights, routes, effects, source timeline tracks and edit topology.
components.evidence: Parsing and preserving an object record do not establish a rendered or editable native consumer.

components.name: Animation & Dynamics
components.summary: Selected source animation and hair-chain behaviors are implemented.
components.available: Generic clip playback, selected normal Animator states, temporal expressions, look-at behavior and bounded original hair dynamics.
components.remaining: Remaining controllers, loop correction, cloth, broader expression/animation combinations and full sequence parity.
components.evidence: Kernel checks, selected frame matches and original-player sequence acceptance remain separate scopes.

components.name: IK & Guides
components.summary: Native solving and selected source guide editing are reachable.
components.available: Recovered solver tests, source guide editing, native handle re-solving, and explicit unsolved-target diagnostics that preserve the pre-IK pose.
components.remaining: Broad GUI acceptance and actual original-player full-body comparisons across supported guide and solver states.
components.evidence: A stable native handle round trip does not by itself prove original full-body solver parity.

components.name: Voice & Audio
components.summary: A bounded scheduler and mixer subset is available.
components.available: Selected source voice scheduling, playback and native mixing behavior with documented timing contracts.
components.remaining: Broader original waveform coverage, spatial audio, lip-sync integration and scene sound consumers.
components.evidence: Scheduler correctness and matched audible output are different acceptance gates.

components.name: Gameplay
components.summary: Headless kernels exist; a complete playable mode does not.
components.available: Bounded cycle, event and ADV execution plus a native headless host that runs a fixed event across save/reload.
components.remaining: Interactive gameplay, NPC and scene bindings, navigation, presentation commands and complete original save state.
components.evidence: A completed headless event is not a completed gameplay loop. The gameplay audit records the executable prefix and remaining command families.

components.name: App & Documents
components.summary: Maker, Studio and document commands form a working native shell.
components.available: SwiftUI app workflows, native document persistence, converted-library selection and identity-checked resource relocation.
components.remaining: Lifecycle hardening, portable data setup, source-aware controls and wider interactive UI regression coverage.
components.evidence: Public CI builds the app but does not launch it; private app acceptance and manual UI checks are recorded separately.

components.name: Math & Scene Foundation
components.summary: Native basis, rig and scene kernels support the application.
components.available: CoreMath/Scene types, coordinate conversion, rig evaluation and bounded geometry/deformation contracts with targeted numerical verification.
components.remaining: Broader deformation coverage and degenerate-input contracts across original assemblies and scene transforms.
components.evidence: A verified kernel does not establish every consumer, model or imported scene behavior.

components.name: Recovery & Verification
components.summary: Public checks and local source probes have explicit evidence boundaries.
components.available: Managed recovery, converters, verification lanes, prerequisite checks, Release bundle inspection and recorded private original-player/app/GPU evidence.
components.remaining: Broader reproducibility, deployment-matrix acceptance, conversion orchestration and complete release gating.
components.evidence: Public CI cannot access original assets. Named fixture skips are not passing source checks. Recovered source, game files and captured evidence remain local.
